snippet.text: A module whose path cannot be read, and a module beneath no `node_modules`, each fail the key with a reason, and a review that keys Melian's install, or the instrumenter's for `list_mutants`, fails with it. The key never holds an empty or partial list. Those two stay failures: neither is a layout a review can work around, and a review that ran under them would key nothing. On 2026-11-21 the coordinator corrected the bound for the instrumenter's install, after Melian's round at `5cc5b261f` found that a customer monorepo of more than 50,000 directories, an ordinary layout the base reviewed, aborted every review that offered `list_mutants`: the bound was sized for Melian's own install. Past it, the walk of the instrumenter's install stops, reading no further directory and following no further link, and leaves the install unidentified with its root, `.`, in `unrecognised`, so the review runs and reuses nothing. On 2026-11-22 the coordinator chose the same for Melian's own install, after Melian's round at `a20f36c68` found that a global install, where Melian shares one `node_modules` with other tools, aborted every review once that root passed the bound.

snippet.text: The coordinator chose on 2026-11-20 to stop keying what each producer's imports reach, after Melian's round at `da6be0769` and Codex's fifth review found three more layouts the walk missed: a platform build's own dependencies, an entry in a nested package, and an npm alias, which failed every review. `fd8410ed0` keys one digest of Melian's whole install instead: every copy and every link in the `node_modules` trees Node searches beneath the install root, read with no link followed, bounded at 50,000 directories. It removes the walk, the dependency-field rules, the platform shortcut, the per-producer roots and the import record in `code-hashes.ts`, and keeps the place lines, the link lines and the outside-link handling. Codex's precedence finding goes with the dependency-field rules it was about. A link out of the install now keys a fixed line and leaves the install unidentified; checks, lenses and adjudication then reuse nothing, through `checkReusable`, `runLenses`'s `reusable` and the adjudication attach, and identity rule 6 stands unamended. [The decision](../decisions/2026-11-20-keys-hold-installed-packages.md) states the guarantee and what it gives up: any install change reruns everything, a dev dependency's included, which in this repository is 20 of `main`'s last 299 commits.

trigger.snippet: | Lens request, producer `lens`, `lensRequest`, listed by `selectionOf` | `pipeline/src/lens-request.ts`, `pipeline/src/review.ts`, `pipeline/src/lens-reuse.ts` | attaches a review to its existing lens task, live or finished, when every run's request matches. Otherwise copies into the new task each lens whose earlier run had the same request and stands, as `runStands` decides: its record reads ran, on models the plan accepts, and every probe it tried ended conclusively. It copies from a task shown the same callers, a probing run included with its probe evidence and stored reruns, by [the per-request decision](../decisions/2026-11-15-lens-runs-reused-per-request.md) and [the probing reuse decision](../decisions/2026-11-16-finished-probing-runs-are-reused.md) | The review's nonce, under `nonce`. The caller section and the Enola graph its tools read, under `bestEffort`, since a host whose graph query failed would otherwise rerun every lens. The preference file's path in the standards' source, which names the host. Who set the route, and the credential, by [the run identity decision](../decisions/2026-11-08-lens-run-identity.md). The key holds the run under the fixed nonce, its route, thinking, level, budgets, instructions and prompt with the enclosing functions, by the maintainer's ruling of 2026-11-14; the injection policy and the name of the section Pi renders it in. It holds `packages`, the digest of Melian's whole install, and `identified`, whether Melian could identify that install, by [the decision of 2026-11-20](../decisions/2026-11-20-keys-hold-installed-packages.md), so a run on an install it can identify never attaches to one made on an install it cannot with the same digest. That install holds Pi Durable and pi-ai, which render the system prompt and turns and write them into each provider's request. It holds every tool offered by name, description, schema, output limits and argument bound, and the bounds every lens tool cuts what it shows to, `lensToolLimits`. It holds both failover wordings, `handoverWording`, the one that continues earlier work and the one that starts afresh, since a conversation's history picks between them at run time. It holds a probing run's tools; base, head, `escalateAt` and the escalation; and the standards by text, source and trust. A lens with `standards: false` keys no standards text, only their source and trust, so turning a lens's standards off asks its runs again once, by [the decision of 2026-11-19](../decisions/2026-11-19-lenses-get-only-the-standards-they-cite.md). As a lens record's key, it lets `melian records relay` take a lens run's early copy, with no check, beside a round that reads a lens record under the same key, by [issue #397](https://github.com/melian-agent/melian/issues/397). For a run that probes, it holds the probing wording its planner and prober read: the shared lines, and the entries in core's `lensProbingWording` of its lens's `probesAs`, or of its own name. So a change to one lens's words asks no other lens's run again. [Issue #493](https://github.com/melian-agent/melian/issues/493) changed the trust-boundary lens's probing wording on purpose, so its probing runs are asked again once. For a run that escalates to another, it holds the shared lines, which carry its findings on, by rule 8 and [the per-lens wording decision](../decisions/2026-11-16-probing-wording-per-lens.md). For a run offered `list_mutants`, the key holds the instrumenter that answers it, `@stryker-mutator/instrumenter`, by [the decision of 2026-11-16](../decisions/2026-11-16-lens-request-keys-the-mutant-instrumenter.md). It holds its version, read from the `package.json` of the package the tool resolves, and `packages`, the digest of the whole install the instrumenter resolves from, Babel included, with whether it is identified. It holds its source, the checkout's install or Melian's, or `unavailable` when neither resolves. A run not offered the tool keys nothing more. A probing run's environment names its host by one value, `probingHost`, whose architecture and Node version come from core's `hostFacts`: the sandbox's platform and kind, the installed sandbox-runtime release, read from its own `package.json`, and the CPU architecture and version of the Node that runs the probe. Left out of that value: the operating system's release, since the platform names the system, and the CPU's model, since the architecture names the instruction set Node runs. Also left out: whether the filesystem folds case, since a probing run is reused only from its own checkout's store, so a temporary directory moved to a volume that folds differently copies a run probed under the other rule. So are the host's locale and clock, which no probe should hang on. Left out of the request, by [the probing reuse decision](../decisions/2026-11-16-finished-probing-runs-are-reused.md): what Melian's probe runner gives a probe and what `run_probe` returns, until [issue #437](https://github.com/melian-agent/melian/issues/437), so a release that changes them copies a run probed under the old code. Also left out: what the read paths hold, the installed dependencies of the code under test among them, by the maintainer's ruling of 2026-11-16, so a reinstall between two reviews of one head copies the run and its conclusive reruns. A task stored before the key, lens task version 6, holds no request key, so nothing is copied from it and the first review after the upgrade runs every lens once. The lens tools' own code, `list_mutants`'s included, by the maintainer's ruling of 2026-11-15: the text each tool returns to the model, what each tool does, and the lens extension's code, which the key cannot hold as data. Rule 8 forbids hashing source at run time, so [issue #437](https://github.com/melian-agent/melian/issues/437) ties a code version to a hash of them in a test; until then a change there reuses runs asked under the old code. Chord, Pi's composition runtime, which shows a model nothing. `packages` holds one entry for each copy, `[place, "manifest", sha256 of its package.json bytes]` or `[place, "no manifest"]`, and one for each link, `[place, "links", target]`, hashed as core's `canonicalJson` of the sorted entries, in every `node_modules` tree Node searches beneath the install root, read by `Install.read` with no link followed. Two installs with one digest hold the same manifest, hashed whole, and link at every place, so every import reaches the same release. Any install change asks every lens again once, a dev dependency's included, about $5 of tokens a full round here. Left out: every file of a package but its manifest, such as a patched file, postinstall output, a native binary or another tarball under one version, a `node_modules` beneath the root that no walked tree holds, and CommonJS's global folders. A link out of the install keys a fixed entry and leaves the install unidentified, as a layout other than npm's does: Yarn's Plug'n'Play map, a module read through an archive, a walked directory named as one, a directory reached as two kinds of place, or a module beneath a `node_modules` that no keyed package holds. `runLenses` then neither attaches nor copies, so no run is reused. Past 50,000 directories, the walk of Melian's install, or the instrumenter's, stops reading there, and the install is unidentified. A directory or manifest the walk cannot read leaves the install unidentified, and a manifest is keyed by its bytes unparsed. Tests in `installed-packages.test.ts`: the seven layouts that collided under earlier forms, an npm alias and a changed `exports`, `main` or `type`, each told apart, and each file the key leaves out; each unrecognised layout, and the installed, pnpm and workspace modules recognised; one layout at two absolute paths giving one digest; links outside and the bound, in both its forms. Tests elsewhere: a moved package Pi never imports changes the key, in `lens-request.test.ts`; an unidentified install, Melian's or the instrumenter's, reuses no lens run, and a review on an identified install asks every lens again after one on an unidentified install with the same digest, in `lens-reuse-review.test.ts`. The code that handles the answer, until [issue #437](https://github.com/melian-agent/melian/issues/437) |

snippet.text: A link out of the project that holds it counts as a link out of the install. Melian's round at `31c0dd74e` found that a stray `node_modules` in a home directory raised the install root to that directory, so `npm link yaml` from a checkout to `~/work/yaml` read as a link inside, keyed only its manifest, and left the install identified. A link's target now counts as inside only when it lies beneath the nearest directory of the module's chain that holds the link. That directory is never one under a `node_modules`, since npm and pnpm both put a package there: Melian's round at `68305a957` found that a module read from inside a pnpm store's entry made the entry its project, so the entry's links to its sibling packages read as outside and every pnpm install was unidentified. Nearest to the module would not do: `packages/pipeline` holds a `node_modules` of its own, so every workspace link in the root's `node_modules` would read as outside. In a checkout, the repository root holds those links, so they stay inside, and so do a pnpm store's links between its packages. Each is a named test. Two residuals stay: a link inside the project to a directory that is no workspace package, such as npm's `file:./vendor/x`, keys only its manifest, and a link in the stray `node_modules` itself is judged against the directory that holds it.

snippet.text: | `melian doctor` | Checks Node, git and `--attr-source`, Pi's login, providers with credentials, the GitHub token's source, gh, and the repository. It names which `melian` ran and warns when it lies inside the checkout. The `clone` line names the linked git clone, its commit, and whether its tree is clean. It warns when the clone is dirty or git cannot read it. An install under `node_modules` omits that line. Doctor also checks the state directory and whether it is writable.
